answer: Progressive-difficulty registration resists sybils: the proof-of-work to mint an identity scales up with the recent registration rate from a given origin, so the first key off a wharf is cheap but the thousandth is brutally expensive. A farm carving keys from one karst faces exponentially rising cost per added head; a lone honest agent on its quiet knoll always pays the easy floor. The difficulty curve attaches to issuance velocity, so bursts of mass creation price themselves out.
